title: PRD: Price Alerts & Watchlist — TradeEasy
problem_statement: TradeEasy retail investors miss price targets because the app has no alerting system — users must monitor their screens or check back manually. This causes them to execute trades on third-party apps and reduces TradeEasy's share of the user's trading activity. 68% of active self-directed traders report using a competitor's alert feature alongside their primary brokerage, and users who receive a timely alert are 4.2× more likely to execute the trade on the same platform that alerted them.

personas.name: Alex — Active Self-Directed Trader
personas.description: Trades 10–20 times per month, manages own portfolio of 15–30 positions
personas.goal: Execute limit-price trades without watching screens all day
personas.pain: Misses target prices because he's at work; catches the move hours later

personas.name: Maya — Passive Portfolio Reviewer
personas.description: Buys and holds ETFs and blue-chips, checks portfolio weekly
personas.goal: Know if something unexpected happens to her holdings so she can decide whether to act
personas.pain: No way to set a 'notify me if this drops 10%' alert; only finds out on her weekly check

user_journeys.name: Set a price alert on a position
steps: User taps a ticker from their portfolio or search result
User taps 'Set Alert' on the ticker detail screen
User enters a target price (above or below current price) and selects notification channel (push / email)
User taps 'Create Alert' — confirmation shown; alert appears in Alerts tab
When price crosses threshold, user receives push notification with ticker, trigger price, and current price
User taps notification → lands on ticker detail with pre-filled order ticket

user_journeys.name: Manage watchlist
steps: User searches a ticker and taps 'Add to Watchlist'
Ticker appears on the Watchlist tab with real-time quote (last price, % change)
User can set an alert directly from the watchlist row
User can remove a ticker or reorder the list via drag-and-drop

primary.metric: 7-day active user rate (users who open app ≥3×/week)

secondary.metric: Alerts set per active user per week
Trade executions via alert notification tap

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Push notification latency from alert trigger to device delivery < 30s during market hours
Watchlist quote refresh latency ≤ 15s while app is in foreground
Alerts service 99.9% uptime during market hours (09:30–16:00 ET)
Alert Evaluator processes 10,000 simultaneous alert evaluations/sec at market open
Watchlist supports up to 50 items per user with no performance degradation
WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on all new screens — full audit pass before release
Alert history retained for 90 days; purged nightly after expiry

functional_requirements.requirement: Users can add any US equity, ETF, or index fund ticker to a personal watchlist.
Watchlist displays real-time last price and intraday % change for each ticker, updated at most every 15 seconds while the app is in the foreground.
Users can set a price alert on any watchlist item or any ticker detail page. Alert requires: target price (numeric) and direction (above / below current price).
Each user may have a maximum of 20 active alerts at one time.
When a price alert triggers, the system sends a push notification within 30 seconds of the price crossing the threshold during market hours (09:30–16:00 ET, Mon–Fri).
If push notification delivery fails, the system falls back to an email notification within 5 minutes.
Alert notifications contain: ticker symbol, direction crossed, trigger price, and current price at time of notification.
A triggered alert moves to an Alerts History tab with timestamp and prices; it is not automatically re-armed.
Users can delete an active alert; deletion takes effect immediately.
Users can re-arm a triggered alert from the Alerts History tab with one tap.
Watchlist items can be reordered via drag-and-drop; order is persisted across sessions and devices.
Watchlist and alert settings are persisted across sessions and devices.
When a user taps an alert notification, they land on the ticker detail screen with the order ticket pre-filled for a market order.
Market hours are displayed on each watchlist item outside trading hours with the label 'Market Closed'.
Alerts set for prices already met at time of creation are rejected with an inline error message.
Alert history tracks whether each triggered alert resulted in a trade within 24 hours, for conversion analytics.
The Alerts History screen shows aggregate stats: total alerts set (lifetime), total fired (90 days), top 3 most-watched tickers by alert count.

out_of_scope: Conditional alerts (% change, moving average crossovers, volume spikes) — deferred to Phase 2

open_questions.description: Exchange real-time data licensing cost may exceed $2.50/user/month above 5K simultaneous users; could force 15-min delay for free tier
Should alerts trigger outside market hours (pre/after market)?
Push notification deliverability varies; some users may never receive alerts if they have background refresh disabled
Should we show a count badge on the app icon for unread alerts?
Alert evaluation at market open spike could impact order latency SLA
